<pos> m. pl.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (v. 
<xref rid="A01794">אַלְוָא</xref>) 
<italic>the herbaceous plant aloe</italic>, a kind of cress.</definition>
<notes> Y. Shebi. IV, 35

<pos> m.</pos>

<notes> R. Hash. I, 1. Ib. 19
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr. Y. Shek. III, beg. 47
<sup>b</sup> bot. בני א' animals born in Elul. Targ. Y. Num. XIV, 37 אילול. Targ. II Esth. III, 7.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A01815">

<entry id="A01816">
<head-word>אַלֹּון, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> v. 
<xref rid="A01780">אַלָּה</xref>) 
<italic>oak.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<italic>—</italic>
<plural-form>Pl. אַלֹּונִים</plural-form>. Gen. R. s. 15 א' בלוטין the bibl. 
<italic>allonim</italic> means 
<italic>b’lutin</italic>, v. בָּלוּט. [Ib. אלמוגים א' read אַלְוִים, v. אַלְוָה, אַלְמוּג]. R. Hash. 23
<sup>a</sup> א' בוטמי, v. בּוּטְמָא; B. Bath. 80
<sup>b</sup> א' בוטני, v. בּוּטְנָא. [Gen. R. s. 60 (play on 
<italic>hallazeh</italic> Gen. XXIV, 6) א' זה he is an oak (of fine appearance); Rashi refers to next w.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A01818">
<head-word>אֲלוּנְטִית, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (אֲלוּנְתִּית) (interchanging with לוּנְטִית q. v.)
<pos> f.</pos> (לוּט, 
<italic>to cover, wrap</italic>, cmp. I Sam. XX, 10, a. לאט in H.</definition>
<notes> Dict.; נ inserted) 
<italic>wrapping cloth, sheet, bathing clothes</italic>. Sabb. 40
<sup>b</sup> מיחם אדם אלונט' (Ms. M. אלונת', Tosef. ib. III (IV), 7 אלונתת) one may warm a sheet on the Sabbath to put it on the stomach; Y. Sabb. XIX, 17
<sup>a</sup> bot. [Gen. R. s. 80 to put on a wound, prob. next w.]—Sabb. 147
<sup>b</sup> (Ms. M. always אלונת', Ar. לונט'). Men. 72
<sup>a</sup>.—Y. Erub. VIII, 25
<sup>b</sup> top.—
<plural-form>Pl. אֲלוּנְטִיאֹות</plural-form> Sabb. XXII, 5 (147
<sup>a</sup>). Ib. 147
<sup>b</sup> בעשר אלונטית (read טִיאֹות …, or … טִיֹּות). Tosef. ib. XVI (XVII), 15 אֲלוּנְטָאֹות (Var. אֲלֻנְטִיאֹות, לֻנְטִיאֹות). Ib. 17 אנלונטאות (Var. אלנטיאות).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A01819">
<head-word>אֲלוּנְטִית, </head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> corr. אֲלוּנְתִּית (אֲלַנְתִּית) f., אֲלִינְתִּין
<pos> m.</pos> (a corrupt. of οἰνάνθη, οἰνάνθινος, œnanthe, œnanthinus; cmp. אניגרון as to נ a. ל) made of the grape (or 
<italic>leaves</italic>) of wild vine (œnanthe), whence </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>an aromatic water</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. VI, 10
<sup>d</sup> he who sprinkles אלינת' œnanthe.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>an unguent</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. ib. I, 3
<sup>a</sup> top סכין אלוונ' וכ' (corr. acc.) you may oint a sick person with œn. on the Sabbath. Y. Sabb. XIV, 14
<sup>c</sup> bot. אלינתין. Y. Shebi. VII, beg. 37
<sup>b</sup> יצאת א' … לתְּפֵילִין (read … תית) except œn. which is only for children (after circumcision).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>a wine</italic> (vinum œnanthinum), used esp. after bathing.</definition>
<notes> Ab. Zar. 30
<sup>a</sup> (expl. as a mixture of old wine, pure water and balsam); Sabb. 140
<sup>a</sup> אלונט' ed. (Ms. M. אלונת'). Ḥull. 6
<sup>a</sup> wine to be put לתוך הא' into a mixture called 
<italic>ăluntith</italic>; Tosef. Dem. I, 24. Y. Bets. I, 60
<sup>d</sup> top.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A01839">
<head-word>אַלְיָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="unknown"> לוי; v. infra)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>attachment</italic>, whence </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (cmp. זָנָב, גֹּונְבָא) 
<italic>tail, fat-tail</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ab. Zar. 25
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to I Sam. IX, 24) what means 
<italic>v’heãleha</italic> (and that which is upon [or by] it)? שוק וא' that means the leg (with thigh) and the fat-tail. מאי והעליה וכ' and why is it called ‘and that which is upon it’? Because the leg is near the fat-tail (back). Ḥull. 117
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr.—כלפי א' (Ar. s. v. כלפי; ed. כלפי לָיָיא, Mss. לָיָא) 
<italic>towards the tail!</italic> i.e. 
<italic>just the reverse!, reverse it</italic>. Pes. 5
<sup>b</sup>; Sabb. 93
<sup>b</sup>; Ab. Zar. 75
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr. [Rashi: כלפי ליֵיא where are you turning to?]</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>ear-lap.</italic></definition>
<notes> Keth. 5
<sup>b</sup></notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A01840">
<head-word>אֵלִיָּהוּ</head-word>

<senses>

<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>

<notes> Sot. 12
<sup>b</sup>; Ex. R. s. 1 אמתה חד אמר ידה the word אמתה (Ex. II, 5)—one says it means אַמָּתָהּ, her arm, the other says it means אֲמָתָהּ, her maid-servant (v. אָמָה).—Lam. R. introd. (R. Josh. </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> א' דבצלי' an arm (direction-post) &c.; v. 
<xref rid="B01093">בְּצַל</xref>; Koh. R. to XII, 7 אם.</definition>
<notes>—אַמַּת (בית) השחי the arm up to the axilla, 
<italic>arm-pit</italic>, name of an opening in a Temple door; v. however, infra. 4).—2) 
<italic>cubit</italic>, a measure equal to the distance from the elbow to the tip of the middle-finger. Keth. 5
<sup>b</sup>; Men. 11
<sup>a</sup> זו א' this one (the middle-finger) is used for defining the cubit measure. Kel. XVII, 10 אַמַּת הבנין וכ' the standard cubit of the Temple proportions was six, that of the vessels five hand-breadths. Sabb. 31
<sup>a</sup> א' הבנין the builder’s cubit (instrument).—א' על א' square-cubit. Yoma 31
<sup>a</sup>; a. e.—Zeb. 62
<sup>b</sup> (גרומה) א' גדומה; Y. Yoma IV, 41
<sup>c</sup> bot. גמודה a reduced cubit; v. גָּדַם; also called א' בת ששה עצבות a cubit of six hand-breadths pressed together (sorrowing), opp. to א' (בת ששה) שוחקות a cubit of six wide-spread (laughing) hand-breadths. Erub. 3
<sup>b</sup>. Y. Shek. VI, end, 50
<sup>b</sup>.—Gen. R. s. 31 (א') תביקין Theban (Egypt.) cubit(?). B. Bath. 99
<sup>b</sup> אמה בית השלחין land for digging a dyke of one cubit’s width; א' בית הקילון (Var. קלון, סילון) land for a creek or pond for watering cattle and washing clothes, of one cubit’s width.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (= אצבע) 
<italic>membrum virile</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 108
<sup>b</sup>. Nid. 13
<sup>a</sup> sq. B. Kam. 19
<sup>b</sup></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition> prop. 
<italic>river-arm</italic>, hence 
<italic>canal, dyke, sewer.</italic></definition>
<notes> Peah II, 2 אַמַּת המים.—Yoma V, 6 אלו ואלו מתערבין בא' the blood of both was mixed in the sewer; Tam. III, 6; B. Mets. 33
<sup>a</sup>; Y. Hor. III, 48
<sup>b</sup> top אמת (בית) השחי a sewer in the Temple called 
<italic>the duct of the arm-pit</italic> (from its shape; v. Grætz Monatsschr. 1880, p. 289; [emendation שית unnecessary]; v. supra.—
